screen.line: 在庫・出荷日程を確認

lines.en: Hello, and welcome to Kamaru Business Japanese.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Today is lesson 6: 25 words — trade shows & keigo.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: First, let's listen to a conversation the day before a trade show.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Kimura, how are the preparations for tomorrow's trade show?
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Our new equipment display is almost finished.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Thanks. Development spent two years planning this product, so we want lots of people to come.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Yes. I'm a little worried about how I speak to visitors, though.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: What matters is manners, and choosing the right polite words. Use respectful language for what the customer does.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Expressions like 少々お待ちください and よろしいでしょうか.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Right. For your own actions, say things like ご案内いたします.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Understood. I'll also ask them to fill in the survey.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Good. If someone asks about an order, check the stock and shipping dates before you answer.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: OK. What if production can't keep up?
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Then contact me. Prices are being revised next month, so I'll handle any contract talks.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Understood. I hear people from shops thinking of adopting it are coming too.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Yes. One company is opening ten new stores next year, so it's a big chance.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Yes, I'll do my best.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Now let's go through today's words one by one. First: keigo & service.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Keigo that raises the other person's actions.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: おっしゃる and いらっしゃる are respectful language.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Polite in words and manner.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Explain things politely to customers.
lines.name: 木村

segments.meaning: choosing the right expression for the situation

lines.en: Choosing the right words for the situation.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Choosing the right keigo is a little difficult.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Courtesy and etiquette when dealing with people.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: We practised business-card etiquette.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Humble form of する (to do).
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: I'll prepare the materials.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: The polite way to say いい (good).
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Would this seat be all right?
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: The polite way to say 少し (a little).
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Could I have a moment of your time?
lines.name: 中村

segments.meaning: waiting (お待ちください / お待ちしております)

lines.en: Polite form of 待つ (to wait), as in お待ちください.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The person in charge is coming, so please wait here.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: A respectful way to say someone has come to a venue.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Thank you for coming today.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Next: orders & contracts.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The polite way to say 注文 (order).
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Are you ready to order?
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: A polite way to say filling something in.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Please write your name here.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: A formal agreement between companies or people.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Next month we'll sign a contract with a new client.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Goods kept in a shop or warehouse for sale.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: This product is out of stock.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Sending goods out to customers.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Your order ships tomorrow.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Making things, for example in a factory.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Production has started at the new factory.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Setting rules or prices anew.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Fees will be revised in April.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: A humble way to refer to your own company.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Let me introduce our company's new product.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Last: products & stores.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Creating new technology or products.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: We spent three years developing a new app.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Coming up with a new plan.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Young employees planned the event.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Machines and equipment.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: We brought in the latest medical equipment.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Laying things out to show many people.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The new product is on display in the lobby.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: An event where products are displayed and introduced.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: A trade show is being held in Tokyo next week.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: Bringing in a new system or machine.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: We'll introduce a new system next year.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: A shop that sells goods.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The store by the station is open until 10 p.m.
lines.name: 木村

lines.en: A newly opened shop.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: A new store opens in Osaka next month.
lines.name: 中村

lines.en: Finally, let's check with a quiz. Choose the answer from 1 to 4.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Question 1. Which word goes in the brackets?
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The answer is 3: ご記入, please write.
lines.name: ナレーター

segments.promptEn: Which is the humble form of する?

lines.en: Question 2. Which is the humble form of する?
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The answer is 1: いたす.
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: Question 3. Which word goes in the brackets?
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The answer is 2: 在庫, out of stock.
lines.name: ナレーター

segments.promptEn: Which word humbly refers to your own company?

lines.en: Question 4. Which word humbly refers to your own company?
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The answer is 4: 弊社.
lines.name: ナレーター

segments.promptEn: Next year we'll ___ a new system.

lines.en: Question 5. Which word goes in the brackets?
lines.name: ナレーター

lines.en: The answer is 2: 導入, introduce.
lines.name: ナレーター
